basis: Gastrointestinal blood-feeding nematode infection with defining blood-loss anemia.

decisions.haematologic: primary: anemia from direct intestinal blood loss is an explicit defining manifestation of this infection.

basis: Branched-chain amino acid metabolism disorder defined by progressive toxic encephalopathy; central respiratory failure reflects neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.neurologic: primary: progressive encephalopathy defines the classic phenotype and occurs in nearly all untreated cases.

basis: Bile-duct, cardiac and vertebral defects define the syndrome; renal malformations/dysfunction occur in roughly 40%+. Posterior embryotoxon usually preserves vision.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: butterfly vertebrae are a major diagnostic skeletal feature explicitly included in the definition.

basis: Progressive vertebral fusion and ankylosis define disease. Skin thickening is reported in 80-99%, but functional injury or destructive skin pathology is not established.

decisions.dermatologic: none: frequent skin thickening alone does not establish inflammation, fibrosis or impaired skin function meeting the damage requirement.

basis: Cutaneous mastocytosis is a clonal hematopoietic mast-cell proliferation producing skin plaques; systemic organ infiltration is not implied.

decisions.haematologic: primary: mastocytosis is a hematopoietic mast-cell neoplasm; skin localization does not remove its hematologic identity.

basis: Dissection directly damages the vertebral artery wall; cerebral infarction is a separately diagnosed complication.

decisions.neurologic: none: associated posterior-circulation infarction is a separate disease, regardless of its frequency in symptomatic series.

basis: Intellectual disability defines disease; urethral hypospadias occurs in 2/3, amblyopia in 1/2 and bicuspid aortic valve in 1/2 assessed patients. Small samples limit certainty.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a structural urethral malformation reported in 2/3 patients; the renal axis explicitly includes the urethra.

basis: Developmental impairment and cranioskeletal malformations define syndrome; congenital heart defects occur in roughly 35%. Frequent blepharophimosis lacks demonstrated visual impairment.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital cardiac malformations occur in approximately 35%, supporting inclusion beyond the single-patient HPO annotations.
decisions.ocular: none: blepharophimosis is frequent, but eyelid morphology alone does not establish impaired vision or ocular function.

basis: A persistent fistulous tract connects the anal canal to perianal skin, directly involving both sites. Associated cellulitis is a separate infection.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the defining fistulous tract directly breaches perianal skin; this structural lesion is distinct from associated cellulitis.

basis: Contractures and sensorineural hearing loss each occur in 30-79%; laryngomalacia and hypospadias (30-79%) omitted by cap. Reflux alone does not establish tissue injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: knee/ankle contractures occur in 30-79% and impair locomotor function; prognathism alone does not make skeletal disease a defining primary axis.
